origin: User-approved-style prompts from iterative ChatGPT STUDY V1/V2/V2.2 design. These are AUTHORING reference data, not completed user learning attempts and not existing PROD records.

source.title: 컨텍스트 엔지니어링으로 완성하는 AI 에이전트

cases.label: approved_style
reasoningMoves: Identify what context was already provided
Identify the missing callable interface/usage knowledge
Compare direct remedy with indirect or overbroad alternatives
cases.prompt: An AI coding agent was asked to implement a user lookup API. It already received the repository folder tree, snake_case naming rule, API endpoint specification, and example response. Yet it reimplemented its own database query and date conversion rather than reusing existing functionality. The real project contains database.connection and utils.py with usable functions. Which change most directly addresses the cause while limiting irrelevant context?

options.text: Add an explicit 'do not reimplement' instruction and strengthen duplicate-code detection after generation.
Provide the real interfaces and usage examples of the relevant existing modules and explicitly require their reuse.
Provide the entire repository code as context so the agent can see every available implementation.
Require a longer implementation plan and self-review before code generation.

cases.rationale: A and D can help but do not teach the agent the callable existing API. C may contain relevant facts but adds excessive noise. B supplies targeted project-specific context and gives the model a concrete reuse path.

distractorReasons.A: Post-generation detection, not relevant missing interface knowledge.
distractorReasons.C: May include answer but needlessly floods context and can distract.
distractorReasons.D: More reasoning steps do not replace absent facts.

hints: Which facts are already available, and which essential facts about the real code are missing? A directory name does not reveal an interface.
Several choices could be useful. Compare how each prevents duplicate logic *and* limits irrelevant context.
Apply two checks to each answer: can the agent call the existing functions correctly, and does the approach use only relevant evidence?
cases.scenarioProvenance: Synthetic developer scenario applying Ch.1 context-bundle principles; mention actual utils.py as scenario information, not a verbatim chapter fact.

cases.label: approved_style
reasoningMoves: Diagnose why actual project facts are unavailable
Assign different roles to plan/status/meeting evidence
Handle conflicts by date and authority without blind overwrites
Distinguish instruction format from access to domain data
cases.prompt: A team asks an AI to summarize project progress, remaining risks and next week's priorities. The model currently receives only a plan written three months ago. Material A is that plan (goals and intended scope). Material B is the latest task/status ledger (completed, ongoing and unresolved bugs). Material C is recent meeting decisions (changed deadlines and priorities). In 6-10 sentences, explain (1) why the AI report is inaccurate, (2) how to use A/B/C and reconcile conflicts, (3) why simply writing a longer prompt cannot solve the problem.
cases.modelAnswer: The AI is missing current reality and team decisions, so it is forced to invent or generalize from an old plan. Use A to define original intent and scope, B as evidence of actual completed/in-progress/blocked work, and C for recent priority or schedule decisions. Do not treat the newest document as authoritative for every field: compare timestamps, record purpose and ownership, and state unresolved conflicts instead of fabricating closure. Build a focused context bundle containing goals, current facts, decisions and remaining uncertainties, then specify a clear report format. More detailed instructions may improve structure but cannot supply facts absent from context.
hints: What can the AI know from an old plan, and what kinds of facts about today cannot be inferred from that plan?
Separate the three materials by their roles: intended goals, observed progress, and decisions about future work. What if they conflict?
Try this outline: root cause -> evidence role of each source -> reconciliation by date/authority -> a lean context bundle -> limits of a longer prompt.
rubricCriteria: Explains context deficit rather than treating poor wording as the sole cause
Explains timestamp/authority-sensitive conflicts without blind overwrite
Contrasts better instructions with real project knowledge
cases.scenarioProvenance: Synthetic project scenario applying Ch.1 context-design and same-question/different-context demonstration.

cases.label: rejected_low_quality
cases.prompt: What book orientation is directly supported by the cover subtitle 'practical AI service guide'?
cases.reason: Cover-only bibliographic recognition; no technical learning; implausible distractors; could be solved without studying chapter 1.

cases.label: rejected_low_quality
cases.prompt: How should ISBN 979-11-7579-005-6 be treated in a study note?
cases.reason: Publisher/ISBN fact; irrelevant to AI/Agent learning objective; must not auto-fallback to front-matter quiz.

cases.label: rejected_too_easy
cases.prompt: A chatbot forgets the previous message because it was not passed to the model. Which fix is best: (A) be friendlier (B) pass previous messages (C) add generic shipping knowledge (D) self-review?
cases.reason: Question reveals missing information and answer almost verbatim; one-step recall with trivial alternatives, not 2-3 step reasoning.

cases.label: rejected_redundancy
cases.prompt: Five questions each rephrase 'Can we infer technical details solely from cover/title?' and two case analyses ask the same limitation.
cases.reason: Superficially different stems test the same knowledge and reasoning operation; not acceptable concept coverage.

cases.label: rejected_display
cases.prompt: Answer appears 'A\n정답: \"A\"'; source shows 'excerptId=; PDF pageIndex=1' and literal '**구절 식별자**'.
cases.reason: Leaky internal annotations, duplicated answer line and missing/garbled citation binding.
